title: Label refinement network from synthetic error augmentation for medical image segmentation
mechanism: A generator of synthetic structural errors plus a label-appearance simulation network makes corrupted masks that look like real network outputs; a refiner trained on image + these masks learns to fix breaks and missing branches.
adaptation: 2D version; error model = skeleton breaks, deletion of the lowest-contrast crack segments, 1 px shifts off the dark ridge, width changes between source conventions (1.5 to 3.25 px), gridline-like false fragments; appearance net mimics out-of-fold crack probability maps; pool cells give extra base-model predictions to correct.
min_experiment: Arm: U-Net refiner on image + 24-class probabilities trained on out-of-fold + synthetic errors. Control: identical refiner trained on out-of-fold maps only. Metric: 5-fold CV crack relF1@2 and IoU, components found. Kill: arm beats control by < 0.01 relF1@2.
evidence: R: airway (chest CT) and brain vessel (CTA) segmentation; beat a 3D U-Net, four earlier label refinement methods and a tubular-structure loss; larger gains with extra unlabeled data (exact numbers not read).
prior_overlap: Crack copy-paste and synthetic half-cut views were data augmentation for the segmenter, not a refiner; mechanism not tested.
